title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: two alleged inconveniences of precise election without obedience-gaze — loves predestined more than justice; kills necessity of faith, obedience, and religious care
pass_a_gloss: They press that we establish that God without the intuit of any obedience has precisely elected some unto salvation: Which opinion they judge to be urged with two inconveniences. One is, that it places God as loving those so predestined more than his own justice, because he wills to save them before he has satisfied his love toward justice in Christ, or has foreseen them as believing in Christ. The other is, that it takes away all necessity of faith and of obedience, and all solicitude of religion, because we say that those so predestined are loved by God unto salvation before and apart from foresight of faith and of obedience in the same.
pass_b_english: They press that we set God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze on obedience. That opinion, they think, is pressed by two inconveniences. One: it makes God love those so predestined more than his own justice, because he wills to save them before he has satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or foresaw them as believing in Christ. The other: it takes away all need of faith and obedience, and all care for religion, because we say those so predestined are loved by God unto salvation before and apart from foresight of faith and obedience in them.
source_text: Instant, nos statuere Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: Quam opinionem duobus incommodis urgeri arbitrantur. Unum est, quod ponat Deum taliter praedestinatos magis amare quam justitiam suam, quia vult eos servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christo credentes praeviderit. Alterum est, quod tollat omnem necessitatem fidei et obedientiae, omnemque religionis solicitudinem, quia dicimus taliter praedestinatos amari a Deo ad salutem ante et citra praevisionem fidei et obedientiae in iisdem.
